back: Regurgitating the cud from the rumen, chewing it again with saliva and swallowing it again.
Largest compartment (left side); bacteria and protozoa ferment cellulose to volatile fatty acids (absorbed), make microbial protein and B vitamins; gases belched.
Honeycomb lining; moves food on or back for rumination; traps heavy objects (hardware disease).
Many folded leaves (manyplies); squeezes food and absorbs water.
The true stomach: glands secrete acid gastric juice; digests protein, including microbes from the rumen.
In the sucking calf it closes into a tube that carries milk straight to the abomasum, bypassing the undeveloped rumen.
Crop stores and softens food; proventriculus secretes gastric juice; gizzard grinds food with grit.

front: Why pigs and poultry need concentrates
back: Their single stomach cannot ferment much fibre, so they need feeds rich in starch and protein.
